Accumulators: exact sums built in pieces

Source: R/acc.R
xsum_acc.Rd

An accumulator holds an exact sum in progress. Add vectors to it in any order and in any number of pieces, merge accumulators built elsewhere, and read the correctly rounded value at any time. The result is the same as xsum() of all the pieces together, bit for bit.

Usage

xsum_acc(x = NULL, na.rm = FALSE)

xsum_add(acc, x, na.rm = FALSE)

xsum_merge(acc, other)

xsum_negate(acc)

xsum_value(acc)

xsum_mean_value(acc, n)

Arguments

x

A numeric or logical vector (NULL for none).

na.rm

Remove NA and NaN values before summing?

acc, other

Accumulators, from xsum_acc().

n

The number of terms the accumulator holds, for the mean.

Value

xsum_acc(), xsum_add(), xsum_merge() and xsum_negate() return an accumulator. xsum_value() and xsum_mean_value() return a double of length one.

Details

Accumulators are ordinary R values (raw vectors of class "xsum_acc", 568 bytes): xsum_add(), xsum_merge() and xsum_negate() return a new accumulator and leave their argument unchanged. Because they are values, they serialise: an accumulator built on a worker by parallel, mirai or future comes back to the caller and merges there. Reduce(xsum_merge, accs) combines a list of them in any order.

xsum_negate() changes the sign of the sum, so xsum_merge(a, xsum_negate(b)) is the exact difference of two sums, rounded once.

An accumulator does not count its terms; xsum_mean_value() takes the count. Special values follow the table in xsum(); an accumulator remembers whether it has seen NA, NaN, Inf or -Inf.

Accumulator bytes are those of the machine that made them. Every CRAN platform is little-endian; an accumulator from a big-endian machine signals a zuexact_accumulator_error.

Examples

acc <- xsum_acc()
acc <- xsum_add(acc, c(1e20, 1))
acc <- xsum_add(acc, -1e20)
xsum_value(acc)
#> [1] 1

# Pieces in any order, merged in any order.
chunks <- split(c(1e100, 1:10, -1e100), rep(1:3, length.out = 12))
accs <- lapply(chunks, xsum_acc)
xsum_value(Reduce(xsum_merge, rev(accs)))
#> [1] 55

# The exact difference of two sums.
a <- xsum_acc(c(0.1, 0.2))
b <- xsum_acc(0.3)
xsum_value(xsum_merge(a, xsum_negate(b)))
#> [1] 2.775558e-17
